lessons.title: 1.2 Reading: Thermal Envelopes & Embodied Carbon Calculations
lessons.summary: Analytical breakdown of U-values, airtightness membranes, and carbon sequestration in engineered timber.
lessons.readingContent:
# Thermal Envelopes & Embodied Carbon Calculations

### The Fundamental Heat Transfer Equation
Heat transfer through a building envelope assembly is governed by the composite thermal transmittance value ($U$-value):

$$Q = U \cdot A \cdot \Delta T$$

Where $Q$ is heat flow in Watts, $A$ is surface area in $m^2$, and $\Delta T$ is the indoor-outdoor temperature gradient in Kelvin.

### Embodied vs. Operational Carbon
Traditional concrete and steel construction emits significant initial carbon ($A1-A3$ stages). By specifying Cross-Laminated Timber (CLT), carbon is sequestered inside the cellulose matrix for the operational lifespan of the structure:

$$C_{\text{sequestered}} = V_{\text{timber}} \times \rho \times 0.5 \times \frac{44}{12}$$

### Key Principles for Oxford Certified Architects
1. Eliminating thermal bridges at floor-to-facade junctions prevents condensation and interstitial mold.
2. Balanced mechanical heat recovery ventilation (MVHR) delivers fresh filtered air while reclaiming 85%+ exhaust heat.
3. Continuous exterior insulation wraps the structural core, maintaining stable thermal mass.

lessons.title: 1.3 Studio Concept Check: Solar Geometry & Envelope Mechanics
lessons.summary: Assess your comprehension of solar heat gain coefficients, stack effect ventilation, and thermal bridging.

quizQuestions.question: Why are horizontal exterior louvers more effective than interior blinds for controlling solar heat gain on south-facing facades?
options: Because they intercept infrared radiation before it passes through the glazing and enters the interior envelope
Because they are heavier and provide structural wind bracing to the curtain wall
Because interior blinds can only be operated with electrical motors
Because horizontal louvers reflect acoustic street noise into the streetscape
quizQuestions.explanation: Once solar radiation penetrates the glass, it turns into long-wave thermal radiation trapped inside by the greenhouse effect. Exterior shading blocks the energy before transmission.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary architectural driver of the "Stack Effect" (buoyancy-driven natural ventilation) in high-ceiling spaces?
options: Air pressure differentials caused by temperature and density differences between the bottom and top of a vertical shaft or atrium
Mechanical air compressors installed in the basement plenum
The magnetic polarity of structural steel columns
The acoustic reverberation time of double-height auditoriums
quizQuestions.explanation: Warm air is lighter and rises toward ceiling clerestory exhaust vents, drawing cooler air in through low-level inlets without requiring mechanical fans.

lessons.title: 2.2 Reading: Circular Economy & Deconstruction Detail Planning

lessons.readingContent:
# Circular Economy & Design for Deconstruction

### The Principle of Reversible Joints
When structural elements are glued or cast permanently together, recycling requires demolition downcycling into aggregate. Design for Deconstruction (DfD) mandates demountable bolted connections:

1. Steel bracket assemblies with reusable stainless fasteners
2. Dry acoustic floor cassettes free from wet screed adhesives
3. Embedded RFID material passports cataloging wood species and structural rating for century-long reuse.

institution: Oxford Institute of Urban Design & Built Environment
